title: The Wright Brothers
about: the life of The Wright Brothers: when and where they were born, their best-known work, discovery or invention and when, a few moments from their life such as moving, studying or a turning point, and when they died if they have. Include several specific numbers, dates or names where the topic has them, some exact and some rounded or hedged (about, nearly, more than, up to).
passages: Wilbur Wright was born on April 16, 1867, near Millville, Indiana, and his brother Orville was born on August 19, 1871, in Dayton, Ohio. Their father, Milton, was a church BISHOP, and the family moved several times, including a stay in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. Around 1878, their father brought home a small toy helicopter made of cork, bamboo and paper, powered by a rubber band. The boys played with it until it broke, then built copies. Neither brother finished high school with a diploma. In 1892 they opened a bicycle shop in Dayton, where they learned to build light, strong machines.

Selling bicycles helped pay for their study of AERONAUTICS. Starting in 1900, they tested GLIDERS on the windy sand dunes near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, a quiet fishing area on the Outer Banks. On December 17, 1903, Orville flew their Flyer, a plane with an engine and two PROPELLERS, for 12 seconds and about 120 feet. Later that day, Wilbur stayed up for 59 seconds and covered more than 850 feet. In 1908, Wilbur flew near Le Mans, France, where French crowds who had doubted the brothers cheered in amazement. Wilbur died of TYPHOID fever on May 30, 1912, at just 45. Orville lived until January 30, 1948, when he was nearly 77.
